desc: Understand the geometry: partition allowed region into corners (BL, BR, TL, TR) and corridors, identify that paths between corners must go via bottom-right or left-top routes.
Derive the sum over y0 and y_mid for the bottom-right route, simplifying to S1(y_mid) = C(R+y_mid+2, y_mid+1) - C(R-L+y_mid+2, y_mid+1).
Compute the sum over y_mid of S1(y) * C(x_br - R - 1 + D - 1 - y, x_br - R - 1) to get T(x_br) = C(x_br + D + 1, D) - C(x_br - L + D + 1, D).
Derive S_TR_from_gate(x, U+1) = C(W - x + H - U + 1, W - x + 1) - 1.
Compute the sum over x_br and x_tr: Σ_{x_br=R+1}^{W} Σ_{x_tr=R+1}^{W} T(x_br) * C(x_tr - x_br + U - D, x_tr - x_br) * S_TR_from_gate(x_tr, U+1), simplify to closed form.
Derive the left-top route formula by symmetry (swap x<->y, L<->D, R<->U, W<->H).
Compute internal corner contributions (BL, BR, TL, TR) using the sum formula S_corner = Σ_{dx,dy} C(dx+dy, dx) (width-dx+1)(height-dy+1) with O(1) evaluation via prefix sums or generating functions.
Implement precomputation of factorials and inverse factorials up to W+H.
Write a function to compute binomial C(n,k) modulo MOD = 998244353.
Implement the total sum: corner internals + bottom-right route + left-top route.
Test the code on the provided sample inputs.
Optimize and ensure it runs within time limits.
